issues: The sprite uses cyan/blue rather than the specified magenta-and-white bird palette.
The enlarged silhouette is a nearly rectangular, symmetrical mask; it does not read as a flying bird at 1x.
No clear short beak is visible between the eyes.
There is no identifiable raised wing or directional flying pose.
The two oversized square eyes dominate the design and make it resemble a stationary robot face or owl block.
Heavy horizontal black bands divide the sprite into rigid sections unlike Capcom's more economical contouring.
Several white and blue areas form stripe-like blocks rather than descriptive feather, body, and wing clusters.
fixes: Replace the cyan/blue with a single NES magenta and reserve white for the face, eye highlight, and belly.
Break the rectangular silhouette by extending a 2–3 px beak forward and raising one wing above or behind the body.
Reduce the eyes and make one dominant side-view eye with a compact black pupil and 1 px white highlight.
Remove the thick central horizontal band and use a continuous 1 px black contour around a rounded body.
Shift the feet or tail backward to establish a clear flight direction and asymmetrical pose.
Consolidate the interior stripes into larger magenta and white clusters, keeping each 8x8 region to black plus roughly two active colors.

issues: The silhouette is a nearly rectangular mask or robot head, not a bird body in flight.
No short beak, raised wing, tail, or egg-dropping anatomy is visible.
The palette is blue, cyan, white, and black rather than the specified magenta-and-white scheme.
At 1x, the two large square eyes merge with the heavy central black band and read as abstract noise.
The sprite footprint appears substantially smaller and squarer than the intended roughly 18x16 px.
Black contouring forms thick bars and large corner blocks instead of the selective 1-pixel Capcom outlines used to clarify anatomy.
Four opaque colors appear within a compact area, making the palette construction unlike a disciplined single NES sprite palette.
The bilateral, face-like symmetry lacks the directional pose and lively mechanical character typical of Mega Man flying enemies.
fixes: Rebuild the silhouette around a horizontal 16-18 px bird body with a projecting 2-3 px beak, a distinct tail, and one raised wing.
Use an asymmetrical side view: place one large eye near the beak and remove the second frontal eye.
Replace cyan and blue with a magenta base and one lighter magenta or white accent; retain black for selective outlines and eye detail.
Limit each hardware-sprite region to three opaque colors plus transparency, using overlap only if an additional palette is essential.
Use mostly 1-pixel black contour segments, opening the outline where adjacent magenta or white clusters already define the form.
Separate the eye, beak, wing, belly, and tail into clean clusters that remain distinct at 1x.
Add a small underside opening or carried egg shape to suggest its egg-dropping role without cluttering the silhouette.

issues: The sprite reads as a front-facing square mask or owl face rather than a flying robot bird.
No raised wing is visible; the silhouette is almost perfectly rectangular and symmetrical.
The intended magenta body colour is replaced by bright blue.
The two equal circular eyes dominate the design, conflicting with the described single big-eye emphasis.
There is no clearly projecting beak; the central black gap reads as a nose or mouth.
Heavy black bands across the middle and bottom make the construction look tiled and boxy rather than articulated.
The tiny 1x version loses the internal features and does not communicate flight direction or egg-dropping behavior.
Corner notches and isolated blue edge pixels create a crude, assembled appearance rather than Capcom's controlled organic clusters.
fixes: Expand the sprite toward the intended 18x16 footprint and build an asymmetric side-view bird silhouette.
Replace the blue with an NES-safe magenta, retaining black, white, and one light accent where tile limits permit.
Create one large outlined eye with a compact 1-2 pixel pupil and reduce or remove the second eye.
Project a short 2-3 pixel beak from the front edge so its direction reads immediately at 1x.
Raise one wing above the body using a stepped magenta-and-white cluster, with a clear gap separating wing and back.
Taper the rear into a small tail and round the belly instead of enclosing everything in a rectangle.
Reduce the thick horizontal black bars to selective 1-pixel contour lines and small internal separations.
Use larger contiguous colour clusters and remove incidental corner notches so the silhouette remains clean at true size.

fixes: Replace the box silhouette with a compact oval body, projecting the head and short 2-3 px beak from one side.
Build one raised wing above the back as a clear stepped silhouette and add a small tail cluster at the rear.
Use black, white, and one magenta/pink sprite color per tile; remove the simultaneous blue and cyan bands.
Reduce the eyes to one prominent outlined eye on the visible side, leaving room for the beak and body contours.
Break the perfect bilateral symmetry with a side-facing flight pose and offset wing.
Thin or remove the central black bands, using 1 px black contours only where they separate eye, wing, belly, and body.
Add a small lower-body opening or tucked egg cluster to suggest its egg-dropping role without cluttering the 18x16 footprint.
